messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Pager: Org=coBALTbridge (cobaltbridge) experiencing elevated 5xx and request latency spike. 85% 5xx in last 2m, errors coming from /v1/generate endpoint. Paging oncall SRE olivia.

olivia: On it. Pulling dashboards now. Any customer-facing impact reports?

maya: cs: Yep, cobaltbridge reported customer-facing timeouts on the sandbox -> prod sync. They're seeing 504s and some jobs failing. They've paused new jobs but want a mitigation.

ryan: eng: Looking at traces — large requests from a single org have very long tail latency and are triggering autoscaling but their token-heavy requests are saturating a couple of dedicated pods. Most traffic to model redwood-v2-opt.

olivia: Thanks. Initial triage: this looks like a per-org hot spike (burst of large-generation jobs). We should temporarily relax strict per-org hard RL to keep customer online, while we throttle extreme requests. Propose: bump org rate limits for cobaltbridge by 2x for 30m and enable short-lived feature flag to reject >8k token requests. Anyone object?

jen: ops: +1 to temporary bump. Also recommend we enable request-size shaping at the gateway to convert large requests into queued jobs rather than immediate long-running generations. I can flip traffic shaping if we agree.

ryan: eng: I can add a quick filter to reject >8k token requests with a friendly 413/429. For RL bump, we have an internal endpoint: POST /internal/orgs/rl-adjust. Example I will run: 

```
# temporary adjustment
POST https://admin.redwood.internal/internal/orgs/rl-adjust
{
  "org": "cobaltbridge",
  "rate_limit": "200/s",
  "burst": "400",
  "duration": "30m",
  "reason": "emergency mitigation during spike"
}
```

maya: cs: Please include me on the customer update if we apply changes. They'll want ETA and we should mention the token cap.

olivia: Go for it ryan + jen. I will coordinate the change and watch SLOs. jen, if you enable shaping, limit to 10k queued and drop the rest with retry-after.

deploy-bot: deploy started by ryan: rl-adjust-service v1.4.2 -> applied to cluster us-west-2 (canary)

ryan: Applied rl-adjust for cobaltbridge: rate_limit=200/s burst=400 duration=30m. Response: {"status":"ok","applied_at":"5932104510","id":"adj-7f3b"}

jen: Traffic shaping enabled on gateway for cobaltbridge: queue_limit=100, max_tokens=10000, retry_after=60s.

olivia: Observing metrics. 5xx down from 85% -> 12% in the first 60s, p95 latency dropping. Looks promising.

maya: cs: I told the customer we applied a temporary rate bump and short token cap; suggested they pause big batch syncs for now. They're OK for 30m.

ryan: Also added short-lived server-side guard to reject requests that attempt to request >200k tokens overall (defense-in-depth).

pagerbot: Incident note: mitigation actions recorded. incident_id=INC-20260503-1402.

olivia: Keep monitoring. If p50/p95 don't improve to acceptable levels within 10m, we'll escalate to fallbacks: route to dedicated spare pool or decrease model size.

jen: Noted. I'll stand by to reroute traffic to spare pool.

ryan: Metrics at 5932104620: 5xx=10%, p95 latency 1.1s, qps ~180 for org. Sustaining under new limit.

olivia: Great. We'll keep the temporary RL bump for 30m and schedule post-incident follow-up. Assigning owner: ryan (eng) for short-term config and postmortem write-up; maya (cs) will handle customer comms; olivia will own incident timeline and follow-up action items.

maya: cs: Customer update sent. They appreciate the fast mitigation and asked for a follow-up on why the burst happened.

olivia: Thanks team. After-action items: (1) determine root cause of cobaltbridge burst (ryan), (2) consider adaptive per-org burst controls / autoscaling changes (olivia+jen), (3) update RL automation to allow safe emergency increases with audit trail (infra). We'll document in the postmortem. Closing active mitigation at 5932104678 once stable.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: rl-adjust-service v1.4.2 applied (canary -> global).
